newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty inches up, no clear trend seen.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty inches up, no clear trend seen.

text.p: The Polish zloty inched up against the basket of currencies and stabilised in early trade after a low opening and dealers said it might not see much more action today because of market holidays in the United States.

"The early easing of the zloty might have made it attractive to some investors, and its subsequent rise might have been capped by those foreigners who wanted to trim Polish positions," said Jaroslaw Dryjski of Bank Slaski SA.
At 0830 GMT the zloty was at 0.74/0.67 percent above the parity rate, up from 0.72/0.59 at opening. Dealers said it was likely to stabilise at around 0.7 percent for the day.
It was at 3.2920/50 against the dollar and 1.8810/30 against the mark from 3.2930/80 and 1.8820/40 at opening respectively.
On the money market overnight and tomorrow/next rates held flat and relatively high at 23.25/23.55 and 23.00/23.50 percent respectively despite a 851 million zloty net inflow into the system.
The NBP offered to drain 300 million zlotys through a 14-day reverse repo and 100 million through a sale of its 182-day NBP bills.

One-, two-, and three-month bids also rose 0.1 point to 22.60 percent on increased market expectations of an interest rate rise after the central bank said yesterday the planned budget gap of 1.9 percent for next year increased the likelihood of such a move.
